cells.tense: What you built by hand over years is ending right on time, and you are here for it.
cells.ask: Sit with a result you brought all the way through, good as it is — no repairs, no next project, just the day you get to have what you made.
cells.core:
You spent a long time on something and it's over — not broken, not taken from you, just finished. The work was real and it holds. You can look at it without needing to prop it up, and this ending isn't somewhere you got stuck; it's the far edge of a long stretch of steady effort. The hours you put in are why you can stand here calmly while it closes.

What's left to do is small. Take pleasure in what came of it — let it be used, let it be seen, let it rest. Then walk away from the finished thing without filling the space that opens up. The work was good, the ending is clean, and nothing here needs rescuing.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it. Now let yourself have that.
cells.verb: letting go of what no longer holds
cells.place: where something has to end before the next thing can start

cells.tense: You will be bracing for the next ending before this one has finished, and the bracing is what hurts.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Ahead of one person who is stuck inside something you've already read through, lay out the way out in plain words a single time — no follow-up, no checking, nothing carried for them.
cells.core:
You read what's ending faster than anyone next to you, and you're already halfway into the next one in your head. From your side it looks like being ready. From theirs it looks like nothing gets to stay finished before you've started taking it apart. The pressure in this isn't the ending — it's running ahead of it.

Ease off by pointing instead of pushing. Show one person the way through, say it plainly once, and leave the walking to them. The release you can feel as fulfillment rather than defeat comes when the ending is genuinely done and you are there for it, not already gone.

cells.tense: Something ended and you are still holding that door open with your shoulder.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Do one specific piece of help for the person still near the ending — lift the box, make the call, carry the thing — and when it's done, be done; don't let it become a standing arrangement.
cells.core:
The ending already happened. You kept the shape of it — the routine, the worry, the role — and the shape is what's eating the hours. What you put into it was real, and that effort is what's tired now. Holding up a closed door is heavier than walking through it.

One concrete act of help, done and finished, is how the strength comes back. Not a permanent post, not someone held up indefinitely — one thing carried, set down, complete. That gives the ending somewhere to land and lets something find its way back to you. What you did there was enough; you don't have to keep proving it.

cells.tense: The clearing is happening by your own hand and you are calling it the natural way of things.
cells.act: let the abundance be seen and used
cells.ask: Keep letting something that finished under your care stand in the open and be used for what it became — show it, lend it, put it where people can reach it — without explaining why it's there.
cells.core:
Something ended here, and it ended well — nothing dramatic, no announcement, just you quietly not refilling what was done. Ask and you'd say it ran its course, and the course was set. The hand that let it finish is yours, and what grew from that steady work is real.

Bring it into the open where you can see it too. Let what grew be used, not just known. Toward yourself and one person who watched, own that the ending was yours to make and you made it cleanly. That's the whole act — claiming the hand that was already there, so the next ending isn't something that happens to you.

attempts.check: The kernel gives no evidence of what the person actually feels about the thing ending, so any core that says they are grieving, relieved, afraid, or unaware of the loss would be inference, not record. The reader could reasonably say 'I actually know exactly what I'm letting go of and I've done it' or 'I'm not clinging, I'm just not finished' — both readings are live and the cores must leave room for either. The asks are all drawn from the listed acts and use the act itself, not its cause, so they survive a wrong read of the person's state; the one sentence that serves the writer over the person is the temptation to name the ending for them, which none of the cores do.

A reader could say 'I'm not clinging, it's simply not done' or 'I've already let this go and I know it' — both survive, because the asks work off what is visible (what was tended, who is near the ending, what already finished) rather than off an interior state. The two temptations in my draft were naming the ending for them and turning the release into a noun; both are now out, and the asks are each one small visible act with a different shape.

attempts.check: The kernel records a capacity — dedication tested by friction, release through Intent — and gives no evidence of what the person feels about what is ending, so any core that reports grief, relief, or unawareness would be inference; the cores stay with the mechanism and let the person recognise themselves or not. The reader could say 'it isn't over, I'm simply still in it' or 'I chose this ending and I know it' — both survive, because every ask works off something visible (a finished result, someone stuck on a route, a person carrying too much, a thing already grown) rather than an interior state. The sentence that served me more than them was the one that had them announce the ending as theirs; it is now a quiet offer with nothing to declare, and the four asks carry four shapes — a sitting, a stop, a finished piece, a continuing to let something be used.
